who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent, lane proofs-1113
task: Prove a property of a whole sans-IO loop (a retry loop, a state machine driven to its end) against everything a kernel may answer, so the simulation test that ran drawn runs of it can be deleted
do: 1. Give the loop its world as ONE value: a trait with the calls it makes and the clock it reads (`wait/retry.rs`: `trait Kernel<T> { fn once(&mut self, left) -> ..; fn now(&self) -> Duration }`, `drive(retry, &mut kernel)`), implemented for what production passes (a tuple of a clock and a closure) so callers do not change. A clock read through `&self` beside a closure that moves it needs a `Cell`, which the translator has no model of; one value needs none. 2. Write the world as a reference model under `crates/blaze-core/src/world/` (`blocking.rs`): its state, `allows(&self, .., &answer) -> bool` for what the kernel may answer, and the state after an answer. Make it at least as liberal as the simulated kernel the test had: check each of that kernel's behaviours is allowed. 3. In the theorem's module write the kernel that answers from a list (`Answers { world, answers, next, stopped }`): each call takes the next answer; past the last one, or an answer the world does not allow, it sets `stopped` and ends the loop (a ready call). 4. The theorem's function takes the list as an argument, runs the REAL loop on that kernel, returns true where `stopped`, and otherwise states the oracle on how the loop ended (`waits`, `a_wait_ends_by_its_deadline`). For every list is every run. Keep a helper that takes the loop's state, so a control can pass a planted one. 5. Run it where it is stated (a `blaze_sim::check` test that draws answers following the world, with `must_reach` for each way the loop ends and for a refused run) and give it a control on one fixed list (the plant makes the function false; without the plant the same list is refused by the world). 6. `blaze prove -p <crate>` emits the models (the loop at its instance: `drive/unit_Answers.lean`); copy them under `lean/BlazeModel/` (H-proof-loop). 7. The proof: one lemma about the loop by induction on its fuel, over an invariant at the loop's head that ties the core's state to the world's (here: the retry's last reading is the world's clock, and it is not past the deadline), concluding `stopped` or the oracle's clauses; fuel is the list's length plus two. Give the lane the invariant and why each turn keeps it; it wrote 290 lines in 15 builds. 8. When Lean has checked it (`#print axioms`), delete the simulation test and its simulated kernel, and say in the test file's header where the property is proved.
why: On 2026-11-14 the wait's retry loop went from a simulation test (400 drawn runs against a hand-written kernel, 236 lines) to a theorem about every run in about two hours, most of it deciding the world's rule. The translator needed nothing new: a trait method on a generic parameter is resolved at the instance, `?` and the opaque `io::Error` were already taken. The proof says more than the test did: the world allows a timeout that comes early with the event still to come, a ready call read late, and a call that starts after the clock was read (one lateness bounds both delays).
